acceptance_checks.description: parsed/<basename>.psv is byte-identical to the legacy golden output for every input, including the anomaly file: HDR/TRL stripped, copybook CBCUST01 slices (1-10,11-40,41-48,49-60,61-63,64-65), trailing-space trim on fields 1/2/5, implied decimal amt/100 as %.2f, date reformat YYYYMMDD -> YYYY-MM-DD with no validity check, records passed through even when malformed.

Detects and records exactly the planted anomaly set to pk=anomaly#<ns> (invalid calendar date, non-UTF-8 byte, short record, trailer/record-count mismatch) while STILL emitting the legacy pass-through bytes. Detection is a side channel, never a change to the .psv bytes.
record_count and trailer_count stored per file in the ledger (retires the never-implemented ETL-0187); mismatch recorded as A-trailer-mismatch, not a failure.
Reprocessing the same object (SQS at-least-once) rewrites identical bytes and does not duplicate ledger items (deterministic keys, PutItem overwrite semantics).
A message whose object cannot be fetched fails loudly and lands on ow-tp-<ns>-events-dlq after 3 receives; no silent-suppression equivalent of 2>/dev/null || true.
No orphaned temp state (/tmp/cb_body.$$ equivalent) and no lock files.
Role ow-tp-<ns>-parser-role: read on incoming/*, write on parsed/* only, dynamodb PutItem/Query on the batch-state table, SQS consume on the events queue; no bucket-wide write.

encoding_policy.byte_transparency: full: process record bytes without a UTF-8 decode layer (latin-1 or bytes API); output bytes re-emit input bytes exactly as the legacy cut/awk chain does
encoding_policy.invalid_bytes: never raise; byte 0xA3 passes through to parsed/ unchanged AND is recorded as A-nonutf8-byte in the ledger

malformed_record_policy.details: Match legacy tolerate semantics byte-for-byte: short records slice to empty fields (amt becomes 0.00, date becomes '--'), nothing is rejected or quarantined from the .psv; anomalies are attributed in the DynamoDB ledger instead. Never fail open on NULL/missing values: they must be attributed, and golden bytes are the arbiter.

empty_input_semantics.details: No incoming/ object events means no invocations; an empty body (HDR+TRL only) writes an empty .psv, matching legacy.
